title: Daily Market Digest: October 3, 2026
subtitle: Review of Friday, October 2, 2026 Trading Session

sections.title: Market Pulse: Jobs Report Fuels Rally, Tech Leads Gains

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Rally on Weak Jobs Data, Reducing Fed Rate Hike Expectations
items.summary: U.S. stocks saw broad gains on Friday, October 2, 2026, as a surprisingly soft September jobs report eased concerns about inflation and significantly lowered the probability of an October Federal Reserve interest rate hike. All major indices closed higher, with the technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite leading the advance. This report covers the last trading session as markets are closed today, October 3, 2026. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Synaptics Surges on Acquisition Plan Revision
items.summary: Synaptics ($SYNA) surged after ON Semiconductor revised its acquisition plans from an all-stock structure to an all-cash deal.

items.headline: Armada Acquisition Jumps on Merger Approval
items.summary: Armada Acquisition Corp. II ($XRPN) jumped following shareholder approval of its combination with Evernorth.

items.headline: Nvidia Hits New All-Time High Amid AI Boom
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) reached a new all-time intraday high, pushing its market capitalization past $5.7 trillion, as investors continued to show strong interest in AI technologies.

items.headline: Integra LifeSciences Dips on Lowered Guidance
items.summary: Integra LifeSciences Holdings Corporation ($IART) saw a significant drop after providing preliminary third-quarter results and updating its full-year 2026 guidance, citing impacts from a July flooding event.

items.headline: Nike Falls on Disappointing Profit Forecast
items.summary: Nike ($NKE) experienced a decline after providing a profit forecast for the fiscal year that fell short of analysts' expectations.

items.headline: Western Digital Among Top Losers
items.summary: Western Digital Corporation ($WDC) was among the day's biggest losers.

items.headline: September Jobs Report Significantly Misses Expectations
items.summary: The U.S. economy added a modest 29,000 jobs in September, falling substantially short of consensus estimates which ranged from 84,000 to 90,000. Concurrently, the unemployment rate edged up to 4.2%. This weaker-than-expected labor market data was a key driver for Friday's stock market rally as it dampened expectations for further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

items.headline: Technology Leads as Rate Hike Fears Recede, Energy Lags
items.summary: Technology stocks, particularly those sensitive to interest rates, led the market's gains, bolstered by reduced expectations of an October Fed rate hike and continued enthusiasm for artificial intelligence. Industrials and consumer cyclicals also showed strength, while energy and financial services sectors lagged.

items.headline: Micron Technology Reports Strong Q4 Earnings Driven by AI Demand
items.summary: Micron Technology ($MU) reported strong financial results for its fiscal fourth quarter of 2026, with non-GAAP earnings per share significantly up and revenues surging year-over-year, both beating analyst estimates. The company attributed this robust performance to strong pricing and demand driven by AI-led memory and storage.
